description: Sabotages for win-pipes-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: What several modes do is not observed, only their values: FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH affects only a pipe whose client is on another computer, PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS needs a remote client to show, and WRITE_DAC, WRITE_OWNER and ACCESS_SYSTEM_SECURITY change what the caller may do to the pipe's security after it is made, which no test here does. A sabotage that swaps one of those values for another is caught by the test that pins the value, and a sabotage that dropped the mode from the call would not be caught for these four. The overlapped flag is observed in the positive direction only (an overlapped pipe starts a read and returns), because a read with an OVERLAPPED on a pipe that was not created overlapped is documented to fail in unpredictable ways and is not made by the suite as written. A security descriptor inside the attributes is not observed: the tests pass attributes with no descriptor and read only whether the handle is inheritable, so a descriptor that was dropped would not be caught.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: the open mode and the pipe mode are passed in each other's place
sabotages.why: The two are both u32s in adjacent positions, so a swap compiles; the direction and the type then take each other's bits.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: the instance count is not the one given
sabotages.why: The count is the one parameter a test can observe by making instances until the call refuses.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: the security attributes are not passed
sabotages.why: Whether the handle can be inherited is decided by the attributes, so dropping them makes an inheritable request produce a handle that is not.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: a name with an interior NUL reaches the call
sabotages.why: The call would read the name up to the NUL and make a pipe with a name the caller did not give.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: the name is made lossy before it reaches the call
sabotages.why: A name that is not valid UTF-16 must reach the call as it is; converting it through a String replaces a lone surrogate and names a different pipe.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: a failed call is not reported as one
sabotages.why: INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE would be wrapped as an owned handle, so every refusal the page describes would come back as a success.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: the overlapped flag is the write-through flag
sabotages.why: The two are neighbouring bits in the same word, and a pipe that is not overlapped does not start a read and return. The sabotaged suite is caught by hanging: its overlapped read is made on a pipe that is not overlapped and blocks, and the sweep's 15 second limit ends it.

sabotages.name: WP-1.1: control, the terminator pushed as an extension
sabotages.why: A control: pushing a zero and extending by one are the same operation, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: a client that connected first is reported as an error
sabotages.why: The call returns zero for it and the page says there is a good connection, so reading every zero as a failure turns a connected pipe into an error.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: a nonzero return is reported as an already connected client
sabotages.why: The two outcomes are told apart by what the call returned; a client that arrived after the call and one that was there before it are different results.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: a pending overlapped connect is reported as an error
sabotages.why: ERROR_IO_PENDING is how the call says an operation was started, so reading it as a failure makes every overlapped connect with no client fail.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: an overlapped connect to a client already there is reported as an error
sabotages.why: The page says a client that connects before the call is a good connection with a zero return, in the overlapped form as in the synchronous one.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: the overlapped connect is made without its OVERLAPPED
sabotages.why: The page says that on an overlapped pipe a null OVERLAPPED can incorrectly report the connect complete, so a connect made that way does not pend. The sabotaged suite may be caught by hanging instead.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: a failed disconnect is not reported
sabotages.why: A handle that is not a pipe instance is refused by the call, and that refusal must reach the caller.

sabotages.name: WP-1.3: control, the already-connected comparison written the other way round
sabotages.why: A control: equality is symmetric, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WP-1.4: the two ends are returned in each other's place
sabotages.why: Both ends are OwnedHandles in adjacent fields, so a swap compiles; a write to the read end then fails.

sabotages.name: WP-1.4: the security attributes are not passed
sabotages.why: Whether the ends can be inherited is decided by the attributes, so dropping them makes an inheritable request produce ends that are not.

sabotages.name: WP-1.4: the buffer size is not the one given
sabotages.why: Declared, and not a gap a test could close: the page says the size "is only a suggestion", so no assertion about what it did would be on the page, and one on what the system happens to do would bind to that. A larger and a smaller size both give a working pipe, which is all the tests assert.

sabotages.name: WP-1.4: a failed call is taken for a success
sabotages.why: Declared: no argument this crate can give makes the call fail on the measuring machine (the largest size succeeds), so no test traverses the error edge. What would reach it is a condition that exhausts the system, which a unit test does not make. A failed call here would take two handles from output parameters the page calls indeterminate.
